_comment: Ratchet down only, same contract as test/frontend-baseline.json (never raise a number to make a red run green; a real optimisation lowers it, and the stage that lowers it explains why here). Pinned cycle 10 (mission 20260903-173653-75d3, aspect P-E opened), the first cycle test/wire-bench.js existed. bytesPerClientPerSec_default is measured by `node test/wire-bench.js` (default mode: 8 guest clients, 5s counting window, deterministic lattice, no Math.random anywhere) against a real server/server.js child booted via test/server-stub.js. Five consecutive runs on this box measured 855.8, 810.2, 815.9, 855.8, 821.6 (min 810.2, max 855.8, spread 5.6% around a ~832 mean) — real quantisation noise, not flakiness: at a 5s window, the FAST_MS=350ms lane expects ~14.3 frames (14 or 15 depending on exactly where the window boundary lands relative to the interval's phase) and the TICK_MS=1000ms lane expects ~5 — a single frame's difference at this short a window is a real ~5-6% swing in total bytes, not a regression. Pin set at 900 (a few % above the observed max, itself already at the top of a natural range) with wire-bench.js's own assertion tolerance at 20% (measured <= pin*1.20 = 1080) so the gate catches an actual multi-frame regression (e.g. a wire-format change that adds real bytes to every row) without paging on this box's own ordinary jitter. The N=60 number (`node test/wire-bench.js --clients 60 --secs 10`, this cycle's actual P-E baseline — STATE.md §6) is NOT pinned here: it is far slower to run (~15s) and the mission's own guardrail 5 says a number needs a repeatable measurement before anything is asserted against it as a gate, not just recorded as a baseline. Recorded reference only: three consecutive N=60/10s runs this cycle measured bytesPerClientPerSec 2638.06, 2613.07, 2562.79 (spread 2.9%, all t:'tick', tick1000 lane p50 ~1.7ms / p95 ~90-98ms, fast350 lane p50 ~95-105ms / p95 100-600ms — tickMs is informational only, this box runs a long-lived foreign Chromium session per STATE.md §8 that inflates tail latency; boxLoaded was true on most of these runs). unchangedRowShare (Task 4, T2.6's opportunity size) measured 0.21-0.23 with riders moving and 0.92 with riders parked at N=60/10s — not gated, informational.
